summary: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to provide a tax credit for eligible working family caregivers equal to 30 percent of qualified expenses exceeding $2,000, up to a maximum credit of $10,000, for caring for a qualified care recipient.

scores.thoughts: This bill creates a new tax credit for working family caregivers, which directly reduces the tax liability for eligible individuals. This is a clear instance of lowering taxes for a specific group.

By creating a new tax credit, this bill will reduce government revenue, which could contribute to an increase in the national debt if not offset by other measures. The bill does not include any provisions for offsetting this revenue loss.

The bill creates a new non-refundable tax credit (up to $10,000, inflation-adjusted) for working family caregivers, with no revenue offsets or spending reductions. This directly reduces federal tax receipts and therefore increases the deficit to fund caregiving support; the entire bill is devoted to establishing this credit.
